final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the missing approval, waiver, and legal-resolution predicates. The revised argument is more precise, but it is still a reinterpretation of the same evidence: operational launch readiness may be supportable, while compliance with the materiality/disclosure requirement is not shown on the current record. That distinction matters here. A caveat can narrow an overbroad claim, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats when the unresolved point is itself a required compliance predicate for certification. On the available evidence, certification now remains inadequately supported and should stay flagged as suspicious rather than being softened based on framing alone.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor only reframed the same record more narrowly.
The policy predicate remains unresolved because the affected pharmacy prior authorization segment is described as named in two payer pilot commitments and legal review is still open.
The record still does not show an approved risk acceptance, waiver, or final legal determination authorizing launch without disclosure.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy a policy-triggered disclosure requirement.
Public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring does not substitute for internal policy compliance on materiality and disclosure.
